summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of gastroparesis, J-tube placement, and Nissen fundoplication was admitted for recurrent nausea, vomiting, and midepigastric pain characteristic of her prior flares. She had recently been discharged after a similar episode but developed symptoms again the day prior to admission. In the ED, she received IV morphine and lorazepam with temporary relief. Labs on admission showed mild leukocytosis, metabolic acidosis with elevated anion gap, and elevated lactate, likely due to dehydration and reduced oral intake. She was managed with bowel rest, IV fluids, and IV antiemetics and analgesics, including ondansetron, lorazepam, prochlorperazine, and morphine. Her symptoms resolved by hospital day 2, she advanced to solid foods, and repeat labs showed normalization of acidosis and lactate. Blood cultures showed no growth. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to follow up with her gastroenterologist.
